content: 1. Cholera is an acute diarrheal illness caused by infection of the intestine with Vibrio cholerae bacteria. 2. Typhoid and paratyphoid fevers are systemic infections caused by Salmonella typhi and Salmonella paratyphi, respectively, characterized by prolonged fever, abdominal pain, and systemic toxicity. 3. Salmonella gastroenteritis is an infection of the gastrointestinal tract caused by Salmonella species, leading to diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and fever. 4. Shigellosis is a bacterial infection caused by Shigella species, resulting in dysentery with symptoms such as diarrhea, fever, and abdominal pain. 5. Staphylococcal food poisoning is caused by ingestion of food contaminated with Staphylococcus aureus enterotoxins, leading to nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. 6. Acute amoebic dysentery, caused by Entamoeba histolytica, presents with severe diarrhea containing blood and mucus, without evidence of abscess formation. 7. Chronic intestinal amoebiasis refers to a prolonged infection with Entamoeba histolytica, causing intermittent diarrhea and abdominal discomfort without abscess formation. 8. Amoebic nondysenteric colitis is a form of amoebiasis where the colon is inflamed without dysenteric symptoms. 9. Amoebic liver abscess is a severe complication of amoebiasis, characterized by the formation of pus-filled cavities in the liver. 10. Amoebic lung abscess occurs when amoebic infection spreads to the lungs, causing respiratory symptoms and abscess formation. 11. Amoebic brain abscess is a rare but serious condition where amoebic infection leads to abscess formation in the brain. 12. Amoebic skin ulceration is a cutaneous manifestation of amoebiasis, often secondary to systemic spread or direct inoculation. 13. Amoebiasis, unspecified, refers to an amoebic infection where the specific site or manifestation is not clearly identified. 14. Giardiasis is an intestinal infection caused by Giardia lamblia, leading to diarrhea, abdominal cramps, and malabsorption. 15. Intestinal protozoa, NOS (not otherwise specified), refers to protozoal infections of the gastrointestinal tract without specific identification of the causative organism. 16. Rotavirus infection is a common cause of severe diarrhea in children, often accompanied by fever and vomiting. 17. Viral gastroenteritis is an inflammation of the stomach and intestines caused by various viruses, leading to diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal pain. 18. Infectious gastroenteritis is a general term for inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract caused by infectious agents, resulting in diarrhea and other symptoms. 19. Primary tuberculous infection refers to the initial infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, often asymptomatic or presenting with mild respiratory symptoms. 20. Pulmonary tuberculosis is a chronic bacterial infection of the lungs caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, characterized by cough, weight loss, and night sweats. 21. Other respiratory tuberculosis includes tuberculosis affecting parts of the respiratory system other than the lungs, such as the pleura. 22. Tuberculosis of the meninges and central nervous system involves Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the brain and spinal cord, leading to meningitis or other neurological complications. 23. Tuberculosis of the intestines, peritoneum, and mesenteric glands involves infection of the gastrointestinal tract and associated lymph nodes, causing abdominal pain and systemic symptoms. 24. Tuberculosis of bones and joints, including Pott's disease, refers to Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the skeletal system, often affecting the spine. 25. Tuberculosis of the genitourinary system involves infection of the kidneys, bladder, or reproductive organs by Mycobacterium tuberculosis. 26. Tuberculosis of other organs refers to extrapulmonary tuberculosis affecting organs such as the liver, spleen, or skin. 27. Erythema nodosum with hypersensitivity reaction in tuberculosis, also known as Bazin disease, is a skin manifestation of tuberculosis characterized by painful nodules. 28. Tuberculosis of peripheral lymph nodes, also known as scrofula, involves infection of lymph nodes, often in the neck, causing swelling and abscess formation. 29. Miliary tuberculosis is a disseminated form of tuberculosis where the bacteria spread through the bloodstream, causing widespread organ involvement. 30. Bubonic plague is a severe bacterial infection caused by Yersinia pestis, characterized by swollen lymph nodes (buboes), fever, and systemic toxicity. 31. Tularemia is a zoonotic bacterial infection caused by Francisella tularensis, presenting with fever, skin ulcers, and lymphadenopathy. 32. Anthrax is a bacterial infection caused by Bacillus anthracis, which can present as cutaneous, inhalational, or gastrointestinal disease. 33. Brucellosis is a zoonotic bacterial infection caused by Brucella species, leading to fever, joint pain, and fatigue. 34. Glanders is a rare bacterial infection caused by Burkholderia mallei, primarily affecting horses but transmissible to humans, causing skin ulcers and systemic symptoms. 35. Melioidosis is an infectious disease caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, presenting with pneumonia, abscesses, and septicemia. 36. Rat-bite fever is a bacterial infection caused by Streptobacillus moniliformis or Spirillum minus, transmitted through rodent bites, leading to fever, rash, and arthritis. 37. Listeriosis is a bacterial infection caused by Listeria monocytogenes, often presenting as meningitis or sepsis in immunocompromised individuals or neonates. 38. Erysipelothrix infection is caused by Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae, leading to skin lesions and systemic symptoms in rare cases. 39. Pasteurellosis is a bacterial infection caused by Pasteurella species, often following animal bites or scratches, leading to cellulitis and abscess formation. 40. Leprosy, also known as Hansen's disease, is a chronic bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae, affecting the skin, nerves, and mucous membranes. 41. Diphtheria is a bacterial infection caused by Corynebacterium diphtheriae, characterized by a thick pseudomembrane in the throat and potential systemic complications. 42. Whooping cough, or pertussis, is a highly contagious respiratory infection caused by Bordetella pertussis, leading to severe coughing fits. 43. Streptococcal sore throat and scarlatina are caused by Group A Streptococcus, presenting as pharyngitis or scarlet fever with a characteristic rash. 44. Erysipelas is a bacterial skin infection caused by Streptococcus species, characterized by red, raised, and sharply demarcated lesions. 45. Meningococcal meningitis is a bacterial infection of the meninges caused by Neisseria meningitidis, presenting with fever, headache, and neck stiffness. 46. Tetanus is a bacterial infection caused by Clostridium tetani, leading to muscle stiffness and spasms due to neurotoxin production. 47. Septicemia, or bloodstream infection, can be caused by various bacteria, including pneumococcal and gram-negative organisms, leading to systemic inflammation and organ dysfunction. 48. Actinomycotic infections are caused by Actinomyces species, leading to chronic abscesses in the oral cavity, lungs, or gastrointestinal tract. 49. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection can lead to immune system compromise, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections and specific conditions. 50. Acute poliomyelitis is a viral infection caused by poliovirus, leading to paralysis in severe cases. 51. Slow virus infections of the central nervous system, such as kuru and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, are caused by prions, leading to progressive neurological decline. 52. Meningitis due to enterovirus is an inflammation of the meninges caused by enteroviruses, presenting with fever, headache, and neck stiffness. 53. Smallpox is a viral disease caused by the variola virus, characterized by fever and a distinctive pustular rash. 54. Chickenpox, caused by the varicella-zoster virus, presents with a vesicular rash, fever, and malaise. 55. Herpes zoster, or shingles, is a reactivation of the varicella-zoster virus, causing a painful, localized vesicular rash. 56. Genital herpes is a sexually transmitted infection caused by herpes simplex virus type 2, leading to painful genital ulcers. 57. Measles is a highly contagious viral infection characterized by fever, cough, conjunctivitis, and a maculopapular rash. 58. Rubella, or German measles, is a viral infection causing a mild rash and fever, with serious implications for pregnant women. 59. Yellow fever is a mosquito-borne viral infection causing fever, jaundice, and hemorrhage in severe cases. 60. Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne viral illness presenting with fever, rash, and severe joint and muscle pain. 61. Viral hepatitis includes infections such as hepatitis A, B, and C, which cause liver inflammation and varying degrees of liver dysfunction. 62. Rabies is a viral infection transmitted through animal bites, leading to encephalitis and death if untreated. 63. Mumps is a viral infection causing parotid gland swelling, fever, and potential complications such as orchitis. 64. Molluscum contagiosum is a viral skin infection causing small, raised, and painless lesions. 65. Lyme disease is a tick-borne bacterial infection caused by Borrelia burgdorferi, presenting with erythema migrans, fever, and joint pain. 66. Syphilis is a sexually transmitted infection caused by Treponema pallidum, with stages including primary, secondary, latent, and tertiary disease. 67. Gonococcal infections, caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae, affect the genitourinary tract, eyes, and other mucosal surfaces. 68. Dermatophytosis refers to fungal infections of the skin, hair, or nails, such as tinea pedis (athlete's foot) and onychomycosis. 69. Candidiasis is a fungal infection caused by Candida species, affecting the mouth, genitals, skin, or nails. 70. Schistosomiasis is a parasitic infection caused by Schistosoma species, leading to chronic organ damage. 71. Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii, often asymptomatic but potentially severe in immunocompromised individuals or during pregnancy. 72. Sarcoidosis is a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause, characterized by granuloma formation in multiple organs.
